literal: The boat called begging, which is without safety, when the rock called withholding strikes, will split apart.
translation: The unsafe boat called begging will split wide open the moment it strikes the hidden reef called refusal.
modern: பாதுகாப்பு இல்லாத இரத்தல் என்னும் தோணி, கொடுப்பதற்கு மனமில்லாமல் ஒளித்தல் என்னும் பாறை மோதும்போது உடைந்து போய்விடும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid nautical metaphor to warn against the dangers of begging. The act of begging (இரவு) is compared to a fragile boat that lacks any safety features (ஏமாப்பு இல்). The act of withholding or refusing to give (கரவு) is compared to a hard, hidden underwater rock (பார்). When a person attempts to navigate life using the fragile boat of begging, it will inevitably shatter into pieces (பக்கு விடும்) the moment it collides with the cold refusal of a miser.
